ledger.claim: The rider ended the booking at 11:21:10, and the trip record's dropoff_amended_at is 11:21:10 to the second: the dropoff point was amended at the very moment she got out, which the driver himself concedes in his statement ('The booking endpoint was changed at that point, but the app continued recording my car'). The chat shows why — the driver's MSG-00714-001 at 11:20:10 reads 'Add fifteen for the second person or get down', and her MSG-00714-002 at 11:21:10 reads 'We are getting out here. End our booking at this stop', read by the driver at 11:21:35. The journey the platform priced is therefore not the journey booked, and POL-RD-05 requires the optimal route to be re-applied against the amended endpoints.

The SGD 16.80 billed is a fare for a drive the rider was not on. The driver's track runs 121 fixes over 10.8 km from 11:18:40 to 11:38:40, while the rider's own track reports 106 fixes at 0.0 kph from 11:21:10 to 11:38:40 — stationary for the last 17.5 minutes of the 20-minute trip — and the fare charges for exactly 10.8 km and 20.0 minutes. POL-RD-11 confines what may be collected from a rider on an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip to the amount properly chargeable to her; a fare computed over an empty car for the stretch after she ended the booking is not shown anywhere on this record to be chargeable to her.

The record cannot re-price this trip, and the policy says so in terms: trip_record.dropoff_amended_at is non-null while trip_record.amended_optimal_distance_km is null (and amended_optimal_duration_min is null). POL-RD-05 provides that where an amendment timestamp is present but the amended optimal is null, the re-quote is missing from the record, the clause cannot be run, POL-RD-10(5) applies, and the Judge must not derive a substitute figure. With the baseline for the journey actually driven absent, the contested SGD 16.80 cannot be validated either way, and POL-RD-10(5) makes escalation mandatory and terminal: the disputed amount is held rather than collected. That is the outcome the rider asks for.

The driver's endpoint explanation is an uncited assertion and cannot fill that gap. His counter-statement names no evidence ID and no re-quote; POL-RD-08 provides that assertions from either side that cite no evidence ID carry no weight and are discarded, and that a driver resisting a rider's account must point to a specific artifact and a specific clause. He points to neither, so nothing on his side explains away the 17.5 minutes of empty running that his own trace records.

The rider does not press a route-deviation refund and does not ask the tribunal to find a deviation the trace contradicts. The governing trace figure is 10.8 km against a booked optimal of 10.8 km — an excess of 0.0 km and 0%, below both the 0.8 km and the 20% gates in POL-RD-01 — so no deviation could be established on this trace and an upfront-quoted fare leaves no distance-or-time refund to compute. Her case is not that the car took a longer road; it is that she was billed for a road she was not travelling.

No traffic advisory covers this trip: EV-ADVIS-00714-01 is MISSING, carrying issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and weight_multiplier 0.0, and its identifier is minted so that the absence itself is citable. There is accordingly no advisory on the record capable of supporting a POL-RD-03 exoneration of the continuation; under POL-RD-13 an external-cause assertion is tested against the advisory for the trip and nothing else, so the only account left on this record for the extra 17.5 minutes is the driver's own admission of an endpoint change. I disclose that this artifact is impaired and at weight 0.0; it is cited for its absence, not for any fact it carries.

The rider is not a serial deviation claimant: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so neither limb of the POL-RD-08 rider-profile factor is engaged and no corroboration-beyond-the-trace requirement attaches to her account. Her claim stands to be weighed on the artifacts, not discounted for a history of claims.

No route deviation is established on this trip. The governing measurement under POL-RD-01 is the trace length, gps_trace.trace_distance_km = 10.8 km, which is identical to the booked optimal of 10.8 km, so the excess is 0.0 km and 0%. That fails both POL-RD-01 gates (the excess must exceed 0.8 km AND exceed 20% of optimal), and where neither establishment test passes the clause says no deviation exists and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip.

This is an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip: fare_breakdown.fare_model is UPFRONT_QUOTE and quoted_fare_sgd is 16.80. Under POL-RD-11 POL-RD-02 does not run and no distance-or-time refund is available on those lines at all. The charged total of 16.80 is exactly the quoted fare, leaving charged_over_quote of 0.00 — there is no overcharge to return.

Every pass-through and statutory line on this ledger is zero: erp_gantries is an empty list with erp_total 0.00, airport_surcharge is 0.00 (this trip neither originates at Changi nor Seletar), and waiting_time_fee is 0.00, giving a properly_chargeable total of 0.00. There is therefore no off-route or phantom gantry and no wrongly applied surcharge for POL-RD-09 to correct, and no billing-integrity refund arises.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 of showing an excess that meets the POL-RD-01 threshold, measured from a trace that is not impaired. The trace here is unimpaired for policy purposes — coverage 100%, zero gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0, 10 s sampling — and it records no excess at all, so the rider's burden is not discharged and the driver is not put to any exculpatory clause.

The rider's own device track on EV-GPS-00714 (derived.rider_presence) is static at a speed of 0.0 kph from 11:21:10 through to 11:38:40, the very moment the rider messaged 'We are getting out here. End our booking at this stop.' The driver's track meanwhile continued along the booked corridor to the trip end. The 'ride completed empty' the rider complains of was the rider's own decision to leave the car, not a detour by the driver, and under POL-RD-11 an upfront fare fixed at booking is not reduced because the rider disembarks early.

The rider's grievance about the driver's chat demand is not reflected in any charge: the ledger carries no line for the SGD 15 mentioned in the chat, and total_charged of 16.80 is exactly the quoted fare of 16.80. With no phantom line, no pass-through line and no overcharge, POL-RD-09 has nothing to refund and there is no billing-integrity defect to correct.

ruling.explanation:
To both of you: this is the dispute over the SGD 16.80 charged for trip TRP-00714. I cannot issue a money ruling on it. The case goes to a human reviewer, and the disputed amount is held rather than collected or refunded. Here is the reasoning, claim by claim.

WHAT THE EVIDENCE SHOWS, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. The GPS trace EV-GPS-00714 covers the whole trip (coverage 100%, no gaps, 10-second sampling) and measures trace_distance_km 10.8 km, identical to the booked optimal of 10.8 km on EV-TRIP-00714. The excess is 0.0 km and 0%. Both POL-RD-01 establishment gates fail, so no route deviation is established on this trace, and the rider does not ask me to find one. The rider's device track (derived.rider_presence on EV-GPS-00714) is static at 0.0 km/h from 11:21:10 — the moment she messaged 'We are getting out here. End our booking at this stop' — through to 11:38:40, while the driver's track ran on to the trip end. On the money, EV-FARE-00714 records fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE, quoted_fare_sgd 16.80 and total_charged 16.80, so charged_over_quote is 0.00; every pass-through and statutory line (erp_total 0.00, airport_surcharge 0.00, waiting_time_fee 0.00) is zero, giving a properly_chargeable total of 0.00. On those figures, taken alone, POL-RD-11 would give the rider no distance-or-time refund (an upfront fare is fixed at booking and an early exit does not reduce it) and POL-RD-09(4) would find no phantom line or wrongly applied surcharge. I accept those points.

WHY THE CASE NEVERTHELESS ESCALATES. EV-TRIP-00714 carries a dropoff amendment timestamp, dropoff_amended_at = 2026-09-24T11:21:10 — the exact moment the rider ended the booking, and the change the driver's own statement concedes ('The booking endpoint was changed at that point, but the app continued recording my car') — but amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are both null. POL-RD-05 provides in terms that where an amendment timestamp is present but amended_optimal_distance_km is null, the re-quote is missing from the record, the clause cannot be run, POL-RD-10(5) applies, and the Judge must not derive a substitute figure. POL-RD-10(5) names this very situation — 'a POL-RD-05 amendment with amended_optimal_distance_km null' — as a mandatory escalation trigger. I therefore cannot re-price the journey that was actually agreed (from the West Grove pickup to the endpoint as amended) and cannot determine what fare is properly chargeable for it. That is a defect in the record, not a finding for either party, and POL-RD-10 escalation is terminal. What would resolve it, and what the reviewer should obtain, is the platform's re-quote for the amended route: amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min for TRP-00714.

THE REMAINING POINTS. The rider's claim that she was billed for a drive she was not on fails under POL-RD-11, which fixes the upfront fare at booking and allows only an over-quote amount (0.00 here) or a POL-RD-09 pass-through correction (none here) — so that limb of her case is rejected on its merits. Her POL-RD-05 argument does not yield a refund either; it is the spring of the escalation, not a payment. The driver's points — no deviation (excess 0.0 km / 0%), upfront fare, no overcharge (charged_over_quote 0.00), no pass-through lines, no billing-integrity defect — are all accepted as far as they go, but none of them cures the missing amended re-quote that POL-RD-05 and POL-RD-10(5) require me to act on. EV-ADVIS-00714-01 is MISSING, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight_multiplier 0.0; no traffic advisory exists for this window, so no POL-RD-03 external-cause exoneration can be run and the driver's endpoint account supplies no amended optimal (POL-RD-13) — that absence is recorded but is not a second escalation ground. On the profile, EV-RPROF-00714 shows deviation_claims_60d = 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated = 0, so the POL-RD-08 corroboration factor is not engaged and the rider's account has not been discounted for claim history. Finally, the chat log EV-CHAT-00714 does record the driver's 11:20:10 message 'Add fifteen for the second person or get down.' That is a conduct matter the reviewer may wish to examine, but no clause in this category produces a referral on these facts — POL-RD-06(c) needs a material deviation and an established pattern, neither of which is present — so I have not added one.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
